items.title: Restricted non-Newtonian constitutive examples
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Chosen generalized Newtonian/Bingham closures; isothermal conformation adds C storage and thermostat, with no empirical applicability claim.
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval containing $0$, let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open reference body with $C^1$ boundary, and let $U$ be an open neighborhood of $\overline B$. A material motion is a map $\chi\in C^2(I\times U;\mathbb R^3)$ whose slices $\chi_t(a)=\chi(t,a)$ are orientation-preserving $C^2$ diffeomorphisms onto their images, with $\chi(0,a)=a$. Its swept open region is $\Omega=\{(t,x):x\in\chi_t(U)\}$, its inverse label is $A(t,x)=\chi_t^{-1}(x)$, and its Eulerian velocity is $u(t,\chi(t,a))=\partial_t\chi(t,a)$. Set $L_{ij}=\partial_j u_i$, $D=(L+L^{\mathsf T})/2$, $\theta=\operatorname{tr}D=\operatorname{div}u$, and $D_t=\partial_t+u\cdot\nabla$. A branch is incompressible when $\theta=0$, so $D$ is symmetric and trace-free. Write $S:T=\operatorname{tr}(S^{\mathsf T}T)$ for the Frobenius contraction and $|S|=(S:S)^{1/2}$ for its norm. Define $\mathrm{Sym}_0(3)=\{D\in M_3(\mathbb R):D=D^{\mathsf T},\operatorname{tr}D=0\}$ and $\mathrm{Sym}^+(3)=\{C\in M_3(\mathbb R):C=C^{\mathsf T},z^{\mathsf T}Cz>0\text{ for every }z\ne0\}$. A rigid observer change is $x^*=Q(t)x+c(t)$ with $Q\in C^2(I,\mathrm{SO}(3))$, $c\in C^2(I,\mathbb R^3)$, and $\mathrm{SO}(3)=\{Q:Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I_3,\det Q=1\}$. A second-order tensor transforms as $S^*=QSQ^{\mathsf T}$; a constitutive response is objective when it obeys this rule at corresponding events.

For the generalized Newtonian and Bingham branches, $\tau$ is a symmetric deviatoric extra stress, meaning $\operatorname{tr}\tau=0$; the total tension-positive Cauchy stress may additionally contain an isotropic pressure. In the conformation branch, $\tau_p$ and $\tau_s$ denote the polymer and solvent stresses separately and the pressure is a Lagrange multiplier. Stress is measured in Pa, $D$ and shear rate in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, viscosity in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, and a rate of stress power per volume in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-3}}$.

For a generalized Newtonian branch, define

$$
\dot\gamma=(2D:D)^{1/2},\qquad \tau=2\eta(\dot\gamma)D,
$$

where $\eta:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ is finite and continuous. Two permitted scalar choices are the Carreau form

$$
\eta_C(\dot\gamma)=\eta_\infty+(\eta_0-\eta_\infty)\bigl(1+(\lambda_C\dot\gamma)^2\bigr)^{(n_C-1)/2},
$$

with $\eta_0\ge\eta_\infty\ge0$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, $\lambda_C\ge0$ in seconds, and dimensionless $n_C>0$, and the regularized power form

$$
\eta_R(\dot\gamma)=m(\varepsilon^2+\dot\gamma^2)^{(n_R-1)/2},
$$

with $m>0$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}^{n_R}$, $\varepsilon>0$ in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, and dimensionless $n_R>0$. The unregularized power form $\eta_U=m\dot\gamma^{\,n_R-1}$ is defined only for $\dot\gamma>0$; its stress is extended by $\tau=0$ at $D=0$, so for $0<n_R<1$ the viscosity diverges at zero rate even though the extended stress can be continuous.

For the Bingham branch, let $\mu_p\ge0$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$ and $\tau_y\ge0$ in $\mathrm{Pa}$. Use the set-valued graph

$$
\mathcal B(D)= \begin{cases} \{2\mu_pD+\tau_yD/|D|\},&D\ne0,\\ \{S\in\mathrm{Sym}_0(3):|S|\le\tau_y\},&D=0, \end{cases}
$$

where $\mathrm{Sym}_0(3)$ is the space of trace-free symmetric $3\times3$ real matrices. Here $\tau_y$ is, by definition, the radius of the Frobenius stress ball at rest; other invariant normalizations require a corresponding parameter conversion. The graph is single-valued for $D\ne0$ and set-valued at rest.

For an isothermal conformation branch, take a smooth incompressible trajectory and a dimensionless matrix $C(t)\in\mathrm{Sym}^+(3)$. Let $G>0$ be a modulus in Pa, $\lambda>0$ a relaxation time in seconds, $\eta_s\ge0$ a solvent viscosity in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, and $T_0>0$ a fixed temperature in K. Here an external thermostat is an idealized heat reservoir that maintains $T_0$ and accounts for heat released by this branch; it is an additional model assumption. Adopt

$$
D_tC-LC-CL^{\mathsf T}=-(C-I_3)/\lambda,\qquad \tau_p=G(C-I_3),\qquad \tau_s=2\eta_sD,\qquad w(C)=\frac G2\bigl(\operatorname{tr}C-\log\det C-3\bigr).
$$

The polymer and solvent stresses $\tau_p,\tau_s$ are measured in Pa, and $w$ is a stored-energy density in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. The determinant is positive because $C$ is symmetric positive definite. These are selected model equations on the stated smooth incompressible regime; they assert no empirical applicability to a particular material, fitted parameter values, PDE solution existence, or universal validity.

items.title: Conditional admissibility of the specified non-Newtonian branches
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Given selected stated law and balances, derive objective nonnegative mechanical dissipation; conformation entropy requires explicit isothermal Helmholtz realization/thermostat.
items.statement:
Work in the smooth incompressible branch of the adopted nonrelativistic continuum model. Let $T>0$, let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $[0,T]$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, and let $u\in C^2(J\times\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ be the Eulerian velocity induced by a $C^2$ material motion with orientation-preserving $C^2$ diffeomorphic time slices, and satisfy $\operatorname{div}u=0$. At a spatial point let $L=\nabla u$, $D=(L+L^{\mathsf T})/2$, $\operatorname{tr}D=0$, and use the Frobenius contraction $S:T=\operatorname{tr}(S^{\mathsf T}T)$ with norm $|S|=(S:S)^{1/2}$. Let $M_3(\mathbb R)$ denote the real $3\times3$ matrices, and define $\mathrm{Sym}_0(3)=\{S\in M_3(\mathbb R):S=S^{\mathsf T},\operatorname{tr}S=0\}$ and $\mathrm{Sym}^+(3)=\{C\in M_3(\mathbb R):C=C^{\mathsf T},z^{\mathsf T}Cz>0\text{ for every }z\ne0\}$. A constitutive response is objective when under every rigid observer change $x^*=Q(t)x+c(t)$, with $Q\in C^2([0,T],\mathrm{SO}(3))$ and $c\in C^2([0,T],\mathbb R^3)$, its second-order tensor value at corresponding events transforms as $S^*=QSQ^{\mathsf T}$. For the generalized Newtonian branch, let $\dot\gamma=(2D:D)^{1/2}$, let $\eta:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be finite and continuous, and set $\tau=2\eta(\dot\gamma)D$. Define $I_3$ as the $3\times3$ identity matrix; in SI units, $L,D,\dot\gamma$ have units $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, $\eta,\eta_s,\mu_p$ have units $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, and $\tau,\tau_y,G$ have units Pa. For the Bingham branch, let $\mu_p\ge0$ in $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$ and $\tau_y\ge0$ in $\mathrm{Pa}$, and set $\mathcal B(D)=\{2\mu_pD+\tau_yD/|D|\}$ for $D\ne0$ and $\mathcal B(0)=\{S\in\mathrm{Sym}_0(3):|S|\le\tau_y\}$. For the conformation branch, take a $C^1$ trajectory $x:[0,T]\to\Omega$ with $x'(t)=u(t,x(t))$. Set $L(t)=\nabla u(t,x(t))$, $D(t)=(L(t)+L(t)^{\mathsf T})/2$, and let the dimensionless $C\in C^1([0,T];M_3(\mathbb R))$ be symmetric, so $C(t)=C(t)^{\mathsf T}$ for all $t$, and satisfy

$$
C'=LC+CL^{\mathsf T}-(C-I_3)/\lambda,\qquad C(0)=C_0\in\mathrm{Sym}^+(3),
$$

where $G>0$ is a modulus in Pa, $\lambda>0$ is a relaxation time in seconds, and $\eta_s\ge0$ is a solvent viscosity in Pa s. Define $\tau_p=G(C-I_3)$, $\tau_s=2\eta_sD$, and $w(C)=\frac G2(\operatorname{tr}C-\log\det C-3)$ in J m$^{-3}$. Then the generalized Newtonian and Bingham branches have objective stress responses and nonnegative instantaneous mechanical power $\tau:D\ge0$ for every allowed stress. On every forward time $t\in[0,T]$, the conformation solution remains positive definite, its constitutive response is objective, and

$$
(\tau_s+\tau_p):D-\frac{d}{dt}w(C) =2\eta_sD:D+\frac{G}{2\lambda}\bigl(\operatorname{tr}C+\operatorname{tr}C^{-1}-6\bigr)\ge0.
$$

Thus the selected smooth branches have nonnegative mechanical or stored-energy dissipation under their stated model hypotheses. This is a conditional deduction, not a claim of empirical material applicability or existence of a fluid partial-differential-equation solution. The conformation inequality is an entropy-production statement only under a separate isothermal model that adopts $w$ as its Helmholtz free-energy density at fixed $T_0>0$ K and includes an external thermostat to account for removed heat; no entropy identity is inferred from the continuum balances alone.

items.title: Resting Bingham graph supports nonzero stress
items.design_state: Step 1 complete draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Worked model calculation/counterexample; leaf, no downstream suppliers.
items.statement:
Use the Bingham graph on $\mathrm{Sym}_0(3)=\{D\in M_3(\mathbb R):D=D^{\mathsf T},\operatorname{tr}D=0\}$ with Frobenius norm $|S|=(\operatorname{tr}(S^{\mathsf T}S))^{1/2}$, whose zero-rate value is $\mathcal B(0)=\{S\in\mathrm{Sym}_0(3):|S|\le\tau_y\}$. Let the strain rate be $D=0$, let the yield-ball radius satisfy $\tau_y>0$ in Pa, and choose

$$
S=\frac{\tau_y}{\sqrt2} \begin{pmatrix} 1&0&0\\ 0&-1&0\\ 0&0&0 \end{pmatrix}.
$$

This example tests membership in the constitutive graph only. It does not assert force balance, a realized material state, or an experimental observation.
